title: Schatten classes and Schur multipliers
summary: Schur multipliers on the Schatten classes of L2(Omega, mu) for sigma-finite (Omega, mu): the Schatten scale with its compact endpoint and completely bounded maps by amplification; Hilbert-Schmidt kernels; S_M(A) = T_{M k_A} with its S_p and cb norms, duality and interpolation; conditional expectations of symbols; the Schur product theorem and the Grothendieck-Haagerup characterisation; Lafforgue-de la Salle's atomless and continuous-symbol theorems; Fourier-Schur transference on R^n; operator-valued and matrix BMO with its interpolation with S_2; the Hormander-Mikhlin-Schur theorem ||S_M||_{S_p} = ||S_M||_{cb,p} <= C_n p^2/(p-1) |||M|||_HMS.

layers.title: The Schatten scale with its compact endpoint

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schattenGauge
targets.statement: For 1 <= p < infinity, S_p(H) is the finite-gauge submodule of TauCeti.OperatorIdealFamily.schatten C p with gauge (sum a_n(A)^p)^(1/p); S_infinity(H) is the compactOperator submodule with the operator norm. The extended gauge ||X||_p in [0, infinity] of a bounded X is the Schatten gauge for p < infinity, and for p = infinity the operator norm if X is compact and infinity otherwise.

api.name: schattenGauge_mono
api.statement: for 1 <= p <= q <= infinity and bounded X, ||X||_q <= ||X||_p; S_p is contained in S_q contractively, in particular S_p is in S_infinity for p < infinity

api.name: finiteRank_dense
api.statement: finite-rank operators lie in every S_p and are dense in S_p for p < infinity and in S_infinity

api.name: schattenGauge_adjoint_comp
api.statement: ||X*||_p = ||X||_p, ||V X W||_p <= ||V|| ||X||_p ||W||, ||U X U*||_p = ||X||_p for an isometry U

api.name: schattenGauge_lsc
api.statement: the extended gauge is lower semicontinuous for the operator norm and S_p is complete

api.name: schattenGauge_le_liminf_compress
api.statement: if finite-rank projections P_alpha increase strongly to 1 then, for 1 <= p < infinity and every bounded X, ||X||_p <= liminf ||P_alpha X P_alpha||_p (a_n(X) <= liminf a_n(P_alpha X P_alpha) for each n, then Fatou for sum a_n^p); at p = infinity only ||X|| <= liminf ||P_alpha X P_alpha|| holds, and the extended-gauge bound fails for every non-compact X

tests.name: diag_harmonic
tests.statement: diag(1/(j+1)) on l2(N): ||.||_2^2 = pi^2/6, compact, ||.||_1 = infinity

tests.name: identity_not_compact
tests.statement: identity of l2(N): ||1||_p = infinity for every p including p = infinity (not compact), whereas the OperatorIdeals p = infinity family gives 1; on C^d, ||1||_p = d^(1/p), ||1||_infinity = 1

tests.name: rank_one_projection
tests.statement: rank-one projection e: a_0 = 1, a_n = 0 for n >= 1, ||e||_p = 1 for all p; a one-based index would give 0

tests.name: compression_endpoint
tests.statement: identity of l2(N) with the coordinate projections P_alpha: ||P_alpha 1 P_alpha||_infinity = 1 for every alpha while ||1||_infinity = infinity, so the compression bound fails at p = infinity; for p < infinity ||P_alpha||_p = alpha^(1/p) -> infinity = ||1||_p

tests.name: zero_space
tests.statement: on the zero space every gauge is 0

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schattenGauge_eq_iSup_trace
targets.statement: For every bounded X on H and 1 <= p < infinity, ||X||_p = sup { |Tr(X B)| : B finite rank, ||B||_{p'} <= 1 } in [0, infinity] (for p = 1 the condition is ||B|| <= 1); and ||X|| = sup { |Tr(X B)| : B finite rank, ||B||_1 <= 1 }. In particular a bounded operator with bounded pairings lies in S_p.

locator.where: lines 638-642 (the bilinear trace duality <A,B> = Tr(AB) between S_p and S_p'); the case X in S_p is NoncommutativeIntegration §2.1 (Lp-Lq duality with the norming element) read through its §1.5, restricted to the dense finite-rank operators of target 1.1; the case X not in S_p (both sides infinite) is this roadmap's, by compressions and the compression bound of 1.1, valid since p < infinity; lafforgue-delasalle-2011 line 400, estimate (9) in the proof of Lemma 1.11, is the form used by 3.3 and 5.2

targets.name: SchattenClasses.interpolation_finiteRank
targets.statement: Let 1 <= p0, p1 <= infinity, 0 < theta < 1, 1/p_theta = (1-theta)/p0 + theta/p1, and T linear from finite-rank operators on H to bounded operators on K with ||T A||_{p_j} <= C_j ||A||_{p_j} for finite-rank A (||.||_infinity the operator norm). Then ||T A||_{p_theta} <= C0^(1-theta) C1^theta ||A||_{p_theta} for finite-rank A.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.cbNorm
targets.statement: For a linear map T : S_2(H) -> S_2(K) and m >= 1, the amplification T^(m) acts entrywise on S_2(H^m) (H^m = WithLp 2 (Fin m -> H)). ||T||_p = sup { ||T A||_p : A in S_2(H), ||A||_p <= 1 } in [0, infinity], and ||T||_{cb,p} = sup_m ||T^(m)||_p.

api.name: cbNorm_ge
api.statement: ||T^(1)||_p = ||T||_p and m -> ||T^(m)||_p is nondecreasing, so ||T||_p <= ||T||_{cb,p}

api.name: cbNorm_comp
api.statement: ||S o T||_{cb,p} <= ||S||_{cb,p} ||T||_{cb,p}; seminorm in [0, infinity]

api.name: cbNorm_conj
api.statement: A -> V A W has cb norm <= ||V|| ||W||; A -> U A U* is a complete isometry for an isometry U

api.name: cbNorm_dual
api.statement: if Tr(T(A) B) = Tr(A T#(B)) on S_2 then ||T||_p = ||T#||_{p'} and ||T||_{cb,p} = ||T#||_{cb,p'}

api.name: cbNorm_interpolation
api.statement: log ||T^(m)||_p and log ||T||_{cb,p} are convex in 1/p

api.name: cbNorm_stabilisation
api.statement: T (x) id acting entrywise on block matrices along a Hilbert basis of L: for dim L = d finite it is T^(d) on S_2(H (x) L) (the zero map when d = 0); for infinite-dimensional L it is defined on block matrices with finitely many nonzero blocks, and on all of S_2(H (x) L) when ||T||_2 < infinity; on either domain its p-norm is ||T||_{cb,p} (compress to finite sets of basis vectors and pair with finite-rank B through 1.2)

api.name: cbNorm_eq_cstar
api.statement: at p = infinity, when ||T||_infinity < infinity, the extension K(H) -> K(K) is completely bounded in the sense of CStarAlgebras C3.2 (cb norm defined only when finite) exactly when ||T||_{cb,infinity} < infinity, and then its C3.2 cb norm is ||T||_{cb,infinity}

tests.name: transpose_cb
tests.statement: transpose on M_n (n >= 2): ||t||_infinity = 1, ||t||_{cb,infinity} = n (flip unitary to n times a rank-one projection), ||t||_{cb,2} = 1, ||t||_{cb,1} = n; the first-amplification definition returns 1; on l2(N) the transpose A -> J A* J has ||t||_infinity = 1 and ||t||_{cb,infinity} = infinity, so its extension to K(l2(N)) is not completely bounded in the sense of C3.2

tests.name: stabilisation_needs_bounded
tests.statement: for infinite d and ||T||_2 = infinity, blocks B_k with ||B_k||_2 <= 2^-k and ||T B_k||_2 >= 1 give a block-diagonal A in S_2(H (x) l2(N)) whose entrywise image has sum ||T B_k||_2^2 = infinity, so T (x) id is not defined on all of S_2

tests.name: unitary_conjugation
tests.statement: A -> U A U* has cb norm 1 for every p

tests.name: diagonal_projection
tests.statement: A -> E11 A E11 + E22 A E22 on M_2 has cb norm 1 for every p (average of conjugations by diag(1,1) and diag(1,-1))

tests.name: zero_space_cb
tests.statement: on the zero space every norm is 0

layers.title: Hilbert-Schmidt kernels on sigma-finite measure spaces

targets.name: SchattenClasses.kernel
targets.statement: For sigma-finite (Omega, mu), (Omega', nu), the kernel operator k -> T_k of AutomorphicSpectralTheory §0.8 is onto S_2(L2(nu), L2(mu)); hence k -> T_k is a unitary L2(mu x nu) = S_2(L2(nu), L2(mu)), and the kernel k_A of A in S_2 is the inverse image of A.

api.name: kernel_operator
api.statement: T_{k_A} = A and k_{T_k} = k

api.name: kernel_isometry
api.statement: A -> k_A is linear with ||k_A||_{L2} = ||A||_2 and <k_A, k_B> = Tr(A* B)

api.name: kernel_finite
api.statement: for finite index sets with counting measure k_A(i, j) = <delta_i, A delta_j>

api.name: kernel_ae
api.statement: kernels equal off a null set give the same operator

tests.name: kernel_matrix_unit
tests.statement: on {1,2} with counting measure the kernel 1_{(1,2)} gives E12 (E12 delta_2 = delta_1); the transposed convention gives E21

tests.name: kernel_min
tests.statement: on [0,1], k = min(x,y): eigenvalues ((j+1/2) pi)^(-2), sum of squares (16/pi^4)(pi^4/96) = 1/6 = ||k||_{L2}^2; k = 1 gives the projection onto constants with ||T_1||_2 = 1

tests.name: identity_no_kernel
tests.statement: the identity of L2([0,1]) is not Hilbert-Schmidt; the indicator of the null diagonal would produce 0

tests.name: zero_measure_kernel
tests.statement: for the zero measure all spaces are zero

targets.name: SchattenClasses.kernel_calculus
targets.statement: For A in S_2(L2(nu), L2(mu)), B in S_2(L2(lambda), L2(nu)), u in L2(mu), v in L2(nu), f in Linf(mu), g in Linf(nu): k_{u (x) v*}(x,y) = u(x) conj v(y); k_{A*}(y,x) = conj k_A(x,y); AB in S_1 with k_{AB}(x,z) = int k_A(x,y) k_B(y,z) dnu(y) a.e.; k_{D_f A D_g}(x,y) = f(x) k_A(x,y) g(y); and Tr(A C) = int int k_A(x,y) k_C(y,x) for C in S_2(L2(mu), L2(nu)), obtained from the one-space formula of the gap on the disjoint union of (Omega, mu) and (Omega', nu) applied to the extensions of A and C by zero.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.transpose
targets.statement: With J the complex conjugation f -> conj f on L2(Omega, mu), the transpose of a bounded A is A^T = J A* J.

locator.where: lines 226-230 (the bilinear identification of S_2(L2(X)) with L2(X x X) through int f g, under which A^T is the flip k_A(y,x)); Remark 1.3, line 244 (duality of a multiplier with its transpose); pisier-grothendieck-2012 Remark 13.4, line 2086 (transposition on M_n is isometric with cb norm n)

api.name: transpose_laws
api.statement: A -> A^T is linear, involutive, (AB)^T = B^T A^T, (A*)^T = (A^T)*, D_f^T = D_f

api.name: transpose_singularValue
api.statement: a_n(A^T) = a_n(A); ||A^T||_p = ||A||_p; A^T compact iff A compact

api.name: kernel_transpose
api.statement: k_{A^T}(x,y) = k_A(y,x) for A in S_2

api.name: trace_transpose
api.statement: Tr(A^T) = Tr(A) for A in S_1, so Tr(A^T B^T) = Tr(AB)

api.name: transpose_matrix
api.statement: for finite index sets A^T is Matrix.transpose

tests.name: transpose_linear
tests.statement: (i E12)^T = i E21 while (i E12)* = -i E21

tests.name: transpose_norm
tests.statement: A = [[1,1],[0,0]] and A^T = [[1,0],[1,0]] both have singular values sqrt 2, 0

tests.name: transpose_multiplication
tests.statement: D_i^T = D_i while D_i* = D_{-i}

targets.name: SchattenClasses.kernel_change
targets.statement: Change of measure: for sigma-finite nu << mu with h = dnu/dmu, U g = sqrt h g is an isometry L2(nu) -> L2(mu) with U* f = f / sqrt h, k^mu_{U A U*}(x,y) = sqrt h(x) k^nu_A(x,y) sqrt h(y), and A -> U A U* is a complete isometry on every S_p. Isomorphisms: for a measure-preserving measurable bijection phi with measurable inverse, k_{C_phi A C_phi*}(x,y) = k_A(phi x, phi y). Sub-sigma-algebras: for A in B with mu sigma-finite on A, V : L2(A) -> L2(B) is an isometry with adjoint the conditional expectation, iota(A) = V A V* and P(B) = V* B V are complete contractions, iota completely isometric, P o iota = id, k_{iota A} = k_A, k_{P B} = E[k_B | A x A]. The same on Omega x Fin m.
hypotheses: sigma-finite measures; for sub-sigma-algebras, mu sigma-finite on the smaller one

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier
targets.statement: For sigma-finite (Omega, mu) and M in Linf(Omega x Omega, mu x mu), the Schur multiplier S_M : S_2(L2(mu)) -> S_2(L2(mu)) is S_M(A) = T_{M k_A}.

api.name: schurMultiplier_norm_two
api.statement: S_M is bounded linear on S_2 with norm ||M||_{Linf(mu x mu)}

api.name: schurMultiplier_congr
api.statement: S_M depends only on the a.e. class of M and M -> S_M is injective

api.name: schurMultiplier_elementary
api.statement: for M(x,y) = f(x) g(y), S_M(A) = D_f A D_g

api.name: schurMultiplier_bimodule
api.statement: S_M(D_f A D_g) = D_f S_M(A) D_g

tests.name: volterra
tests.statement: on [0,1], M = 1_{x<y} and A the projection onto constants: S_M(A) is g -> int_x^1 g with ||.||_2^2 = 1/2

tests.name: diagonal_null
tests.statement: on [0,1] the symbol 1_{x=y} is 0 a.e. so S_M = 0

tests.name: zero_measure_mult
tests.statement: for the zero measure S_M = 0 and ||M||_inf = 0

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_algebra
targets.statement: S_{MN} = S_M S_N, S_{M+N} = S_M + S_N, S_{cM} = c S_M, S_1 = id; the adjoint of S_M for the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product Tr(A* B) is S_{conj M}; ||S_M||_{S2->S2} = ||M||_inf; hence M -> S_M is an isometric unital *-homomorphism from Linf(mu x mu) with pointwise conjugation into B(S_2). Moreover S_M(A)* = S_{Mtilde}(A*) with Mtilde(x,y) = conj M(y,x), and S_M(A)^T = S_{M^t}(A^T).
hypotheses: M, N in Linf(mu x mu)

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_norm_eq
targets.statement: For 1 <= p <= infinity, ||S_M||_p (target 1.4) equals the supremum over finite-rank A with ||A||_p <= 1 and equals sup |Tr(S_M(A) B)| over finite-rank A, B with ||A||_p <= 1, ||B||_{p'} <= 1; S_2 cap S_p is dense in S_p (in S_infinity at p = infinity) so a finite norm gives a unique bounded extension S_p -> S_p; ||S_{f(x)g(y)}||_p <= ||f||_inf ||g||_inf; if M_k -> M a.e. with sup ||M_k||_inf < infinity then ||S_M||_p <= liminf ||S_{M_k}||_p (and for cb norms); the norms depend only on the a.e. class.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_finite
targets.statement: For a finite type iota with counting measure: L2(iota) = EuclideanSpace C iota, S_2 = Matrix iota iota C (via Matrix.toEuclideanCLM), k_A(i,j) = A i j, S_M(A) = M hadamard A, ||S_M||_p is the norm of A -> M hadamard A for TauCeti.UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm.schatten at exponent p, and the amplified symbol M_m is the Kronecker product of M with the all-ones m x m matrix.
hypotheses: iota finite type with counting measure

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_cbNorm
targets.statement: For m >= 1 the amplified symbol M_m(x,i,y,j) = M(x,y) on Omega x Fin m with mu x counting measure, and ||S_M||_{cb,p} = sup_m ||S_{M_m}||_p in [0, infinity].

api.name: cbNorm_eq_amplification
api.statement: S_{M_m} is the amplification (S_M)^(m) of target 1.4 through L2(Omega x Fin m) = L2(Omega)^m, so ||S_M||_{cb,p} is the cb norm of target 1.4

api.name: norm_le_cbNorm
api.statement: ||S_M||_p <= ||S_M||_{cb,p}; m -> ||S_{M_m}||_p nondecreasing

tests.name: cb_identity
tests.statement: M = 1: S_{M_m} is the identity of S_2(H^m); the alternative M(x,y) delta_ij gives the block-diagonal pinching, not the amplification of the identity

tests.name: cb_zero_measure
tests.statement: for the zero measure all norms are 0

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_stabilisation
targets.statement: With M_inf(x,i,y,j) = M(x,y) on Omega x N: ||S_M||_{cb,p} = ||S_{M_inf}||_{cb,p} = ||S_{M_inf}||_p. For sigma-finite (Omega', nu) and M'(x,w,y,w') = M(x,y): ||S_{M'}||_{cb,p} = ||S_M||_{cb,p}, ||S_{M'}||_p = ||S_M||_{cb,p} when L2(nu) is infinite-dimensional and = ||S_{M_d}||_p when it has dimension d. At p = infinity, when ||S_M||_infinity < infinity, the extension of S_M to K(H) is completely bounded in the sense of CStarAlgebras C3.2 exactly when ||S_M||_{cb,infinity} < infinity, with C3.2 cb norm ||S_M||_{cb,infinity}.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_invariance
targets.statement: For the norms and the cb norms: invariance under measure-preserving isomorphisms; for sigma-finite nu << mu the norms for nu are at most those for mu, equal for equivalent measures; restriction to E x E does not increase them; ||S_{M^t}||_p = ||S_{conj M}||_p = ||S_M||_p, likewise for cb norms.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_dual
targets.statement: Tr(S_M(A) B) = Tr(A S_{M^t}(B)) for A, B in S_2; hence ||S_M||_p = ||S_{M^t}||_{p'} = ||S_M||_{p'} and ||S_M||_{cb,p} = ||S_{M^t}||_{cb,p'} = ||S_M||_{cb,p'} for every 1 <= p <= infinity.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_interpolation
targets.statement: For 1 <= p0, p1 <= infinity, ||S_M||_{p_theta} <= ||S_M||_{p0}^(1-theta) ||S_M||_{p1}^theta and the same for cb norms; if |1/p - 1/2| <= |1/q - 1/2| then ||S_M||_p <= ||S_M||_q and ||S_M||_{cb,p} <= ||S_M||_{cb,q}; in particular ||M||_inf = ||S_M||_2 <= ||S_M||_p <= ||S_M||_infinity, and ||S_M||_p <= ||S_M||_q for 2 <= p <= q <= infinity.

locator.where: Remark 1.4, lines 246-252 (interpolation identity with p and q exchanged in the source, line 249)

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_weakStar
targets.statement: If ||S_M||_infinity < infinity there is a unique weak-* continuous map on B(H) = S_1(H)* agreeing with S_M on S_2: the adjoint of S_{M^t} on S_1, of norm ||S_M||_infinity, bimodular over Linf(mu), multiplicative in the symbol, completely bounded in the sense of CStarAlgebras C3.2 exactly when ||S_M||_{cb,infinity} < infinity, with cb norm ||S_M||_{cb,infinity}.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_condExp_le
targets.statement: For sigma-algebras A in B on Omega with mu sigma-finite on A and phi in Linf(B x B): ||E[phi | A x A]||_{S_p(L2(A))} <= ||phi||_{S_p(L2(B))} and the same for cb norms; and Tr(S_phi(iota A) iota B) = Tr(S_{E[phi|A x A]}(A) B) for A, B in S_2(L2(A)).

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_martingale
targets.statement: For a directed family (B_alpha) of sub-sigma-algebras, mu sigma-finite on each, generating B, and f in Linf(B x B) with f_alpha = E[f | B_alpha x B_alpha]: ||f||_{S_p(L2(B))} = sup_alpha ||f_alpha||_{S_p(L2(B_alpha))}, the net nondecreasing; the same for cb norms.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_cbNorm_sigmaAlgebra
targets.statement: For phi in Linf(A x A): ||phi||_{cb, S_p(L2(A))} = ||phi||_{cb, S_p(L2(B))}; hence ||E[phi | A x A]||_{cb, S_p(L2(B))} <= ||phi||_{cb, S_p(L2(B))} for phi in Linf(B x B).

layers.title: Positive symbols and the Grothendieck-Haagerup characterisation

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurProduct
targets.statement: For a finite type iota and M in Matrix iota iota C the following are equivalent: M is positive semidefinite; A -> M hadamard A is positive; it is completely positive (CompletelyPositiveMap on CStarMatrix iota iota C). When they hold, ||S_M||_p = ||S_M||_{cb,p} = max_j M(j,j) for every 1 <= p <= infinity (0 for empty iota).

locator.where: Ch. 5 (uncertified); paulsen-2002 Ch. 3 and Ch. 8 (uncertified); pisier-grothendieck-2012 lines 767-772

targets.name: SchattenClasses.haagerupNorm
targets.statement: ||M||_H = inf { ||xi||_{Linf(mu;K)} ||eta||_{Linf(mu;K)} } over separable complex Hilbert spaces K and strongly measurable xi, eta : Omega -> K with M(x,y) = <xi(x), eta(y)> for mu x mu-a.e. (x,y); inf of the empty set is infinity.

locator.where: Theorem 1.7, lines 274-278; cgpt-2023 lines 89-93; pisier-grothendieck-2012 (3.9), line 656

api.name: haagerupNorm_lp
api.statement: the infimum is unchanged when K is restricted to l2(N)

api.name: haagerupNorm_laws
api.statement: depends only on the class; ||M||_inf <= ||M||_H; subadditive; submultiplicative under pointwise products; ||M^t||_H = ||conj M||_H = ||M||_H; ||f (x) g||_H = ||f||_inf ||g||_inf

api.name: haagerupNorm_invariance
api.statement: invariant under equivalent measures and measure-preserving isomorphisms

api.name: haagerupNorm_attained
api.statement: for finite iota the infimum is attained with dim K <= 2 |iota|

tests.name: haagerup_constant_N
tests.statement: constant 1 on N with counting measure: ||1||_H = 1 (K = C); the variant with L2 norms of xi, eta gives infinity

tests.name: haagerup_diagonal
tests.statement: 1_{i=j} on N: xi_i = eta_i = e_i gives ||.||_H = 1

targets.name: SchattenClasses.grothendieckHaagerup_finite
targets.statement: For a finite type iota and M in Matrix iota iota C: ||S_M||_infinity = ||S_M||_{cb,infinity} = ||S_M||_1 = ||S_M||_{cb,1} = ||M||_H, the infimum attained.

locator.where: Proposition 3.3, line 781; Remark 13.4, line 2086; (3.9)-(3.10), lines 656-665; Remark 23.4, line 3541; Lemma 23.1, line 3439

targets.name: SchattenClasses.grothendieckHaagerup
targets.statement: For sigma-finite (Omega, mu) and M in Linf(mu x mu): ||S_M||_infinity = ||S_M||_{cb,infinity} = ||S_M||_1 = ||S_M||_{cb,1} = ||M||_H in [0, infinity].

locator.where: Theorem 1.7, line 274; proof lines 286-337; cgpt-2023 lines 89-94

targets.name: SchattenClasses.Atomless
targets.statement: A measure mu is atomless when no set is an atom in the sense of MeasureTheory.Measure.IsAtom (measurable, positive measure, every measurable subset null or of full measure).
hypotheses: mu a measure on a measurable space

api.name: atom_finite
api.statement: a sigma-finite atom has finite measure; atomlessness of sigma-finite measures is invariant under equivalence, measure-preserving isomorphisms, restriction, and products with sigma-finite measures

api.name: sierpinski
api.statement: if mu is atomless, A measurable with mu(A) < infinity and 0 <= t <= mu(A), there is a measurable B in A with mu(B) = t; hence equal-measure n-partitions

api.name: atomless_iff_nullSingleton
api.statement: on a standard Borel space a sigma-finite measure is atomless iff it has null singletons

tests.name: lebesgue_atomless
tests.statement: Lebesgue measure on [0,1] is atomless; counting measure on {1,2} has atoms {1}, {2}; delta_0 + Lebesgue has the atom {0}

tests.name: cocountable
tests.statement: the countable-cocountable measure on an uncountable set has null singletons (NullSingletonClass) but the whole space is an atom

tests.name: zero_measure_atomless
tests.statement: the zero measure is atomless

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_condExp_equalMass
targets.statement: Let A in B be finite sigma-algebras on Omega and mu a finite measure on B such that every minimal nonempty set of A is a union of minimal nonempty sets of B of equal measure. Then ||E[phi | A x A]||_{S_p(L2(B))} <= ||phi||_{S_p(L2(B))} for every B x B-measurable phi and 1 <= p <= infinity.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_norm_eq_cbNorm_of_atomless
targets.statement: For an atomless sigma-finite (Omega, mu), every M in Linf(mu x mu) and every 1 <= p <= infinity: ||S_M||_p = ||S_M||_{cb,p}.

locator.where: Theorem 1.18, line 505; proof lines 508-520; cgpt-2023 line 231

layers.title: Continuous symbols on Radon measure spaces

targets.name: SchattenClasses.exists_finitelySupported_approx
targets.statement: For a finite Radon measure mu on a locally compact Hausdorff space X there is a net of finitely supported measures sum c_i delta_{x_i} with c_i >= 0 and x_i in supp mu such that int F d(mu_alpha x mu_alpha) -> int F d(mu x mu) for every continuous compactly supported F on X x X and int f dmu_alpha -> int f dmu for every continuous compactly supported f on X.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_continuous
targets.statement: Let X be locally compact Hausdorff, mu a sigma-finite Radon measure, M : X x X -> C continuous, 1 <= p <= infinity, C a finite real >= 0. Then M is mu x mu-essentially bounded with ||S_M||_p <= C iff for every finite Sigma in supp mu the matrix multiplier (M(s,t))_{s,t in Sigma} on S_p(l2(Sigma)) has norm <= C; the same for cb norms. Hence the norms depend only on supp mu, and if supp mu has no isolated point then ||S_M||_p = ||S_M||_{cb,p}.

locator.where: Theorem 1.19, line 524; proof lines 535-588; cgpt-2023 lines 232-237; caspers-delasalle-2015 Theorem 3.1, line 282

layers.title: Toeplitz symbols and Fourier-Schur transference on R^n

targets.name: SchattenClasses.toeplitzSymbol
targets.statement: For m in Linf(R^n), the Toeplitz symbol M_m(x,y) = m(x - y) as a class in Linf(R^n x R^n) (well defined since (x,y) -> (x - y, y) is measure preserving).

locator.where: lines 59-66; caspers-delasalle-2015 lines 28-30; lafforgue-delasalle-2011 Notation 2.1, line 597

api.name: toeplitzSymbol_algebra
api.statement: ||M_m||_inf = ||m||_inf; M_{m1 m2} = M_{m1} M_{m2}; (M_m)^t = M_{m(-.)}; conj M_m = M_{conj m}

api.name: toeplitz_covariance
api.statement: S_{M_m} commutes with conjugation by translations and modulations; S_{M_{m(.-t)}}(A) = V_t^{-1} S_{M_m}(V_t A) for V_t f = f(. + t), so symbol translates have the same norms; dilations preserve the norms

api.name: toeplitz_mollify
api.statement: for a probability density rho, ||S_{M_{m*rho}}||_{(cb),p} <= ||S_{M_m}||_{(cb),p}

tests.name: toeplitz_character
tests.statement: m = e_a: S_{M_m}(A) = D_{e_a} A D_{e_a}*, norm and cb norm 1

tests.name: toeplitz_cos
tests.statement: m = cos(2 pi <a,.>): xi(x) = eta(x) = (e_a(x), e_{-a}(x))/sqrt 2 gives <xi(x),eta(y)> = cos(2 pi <a, x - y>), so ||S_{M_m}||_infinity = 1

targets.name: SchattenClasses.fourierMultiplier_cbNorm
targets.statement: For k >= 1, T_m^(k) is MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierMultiplierCLM F_k m on L2(R^n; F_k), F_k the k x k matrices with the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product; ||T_m^(k)||_p = sup { ||T_m^(k) f||_{Lp(S_p^k)} : f in L2(R^n; F_k), ||f||_{Lp(S_p^k)} <= 1 } with the pointwise norm TauCeti.UnitarilyInvariantSeminorm.schatten; ||T_m||_p = ||T_m^(1)||_p and ||T_m||_{cb,p} = sup_k ||T_m^(k)||_p.

locator.where: lines 60-74 and 250-251; caspers-delasalle-2015 lines 26-41; lafforgue-delasalle-2011 (3), lines 193-199

api.name: fourierMultiplier_cb_ge
api.statement: ||T_m||_p <= ||T_m||_{cb,p}; k -> ||T_m^(k)||_p nondecreasing

api.name: fourierMultiplier_modulation
api.statement: T_m(e_s f) = e_s T_{m(.+s)} f; R T_m R = T_{m(-.)} for the reflection R; dilations preserve norms

api.name: fourierMultiplier_dual
api.statement: ||T_m||_{(cb),p} = ||T_m||_{(cb),p'} since the transpose of T_m for int tr(f g) is T_{m(-.)}

api.name: fourierMultiplier_mollify
api.statement: ||T_{m*rho}||_{(cb),p} <= ||T_m||_{(cb),p}; norms lower semicontinuous under boundedly a.e. convergent symbols

tests.name: fourier_character
tests.statement: m = e_a: T_m f = f(. + a), a complete isometry; the opposite convention gives f(. - a)

tests.name: fourier_cos
tests.statement: m = cos(2 pi <a,.>): T_m = (V_a + V_{-a})/2, norm 1 at p = 1 (nonnegative f) and at most 1 for every p

tests.name: fourier_trivial
tests.statement: m = 1: all norms 1; m = 0: all norms 0

targets.name: SchattenClasses.folnerCompression
targets.statement: For g in L2(R^n; F_k) and bounded measurable F of positive measure, Lambda_F(g) is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator on L2(F) (x) C^k with kernel 1_F(s) (F^{-1} g)(s - t) 1_F(t). Then ||Lambda_F(g)||_p <= |F|^(1/p) ||g||_{Lp(S_p^k)} for g in L1 cap Linf; |Q_R|^{-1} Tr(Lambda_{Q_R}(g) Lambda_{Q_R}(h)) -> int tr(g h); ||g||_{Lp(S_p^k)} <= liminf |Q_R|^{-1/p} ||Lambda_{Q_R}(g)||_p for g in L2, with equality and a limit for g in L1 cap Linf; and Lambda_F(F(m F^{-1} g)) = S_{M_m}(Lambda_F(g)).

api.name: folner_pairing
api.statement: |Q_R|^{-1} Tr(Lambda(g) Lambda(h)) -> int tr(g h)

api.name: folner_lower
api.statement: ||g||_p <= liminf |Q_R|^{-1/p} ||Lambda_{Q_R}(g)||_p

api.name: folner_intertwine
api.statement: Lambda_F(F(m F^{-1} g)) = S_{M_m}(Lambda_F(g))

tests.name: folner_two
tests.statement: ||Lambda_F(g)||_2^2 = int |g check(u)|^2 |F cap (F+u)| du <= |F| ||g||_2^2: normalisation |F|^(1/2); |F|^{-1} would give 0 in the limit

tests.name: folner_translate
tests.statement: Lambda_F(g(. - a)) = D_{e_a} Lambda_F(g) D_{e_a}*

targets.name: SchattenClasses.fourierSide_approxIdentity
targets.statement: For 1 <= p <= infinity there are f_R in L2 cap Lp, g_R in L2 cap Lp' with ||f_R||_p = ||g_R||_{p'} = 1, nonnegative even Fourier transforms and int (T_m f_R) g_R -> m(0) for every bounded m continuous at 0. Hence for m bounded continuous, s_1..s_N in R^n, a in S_p^N(S_p^k), b in S_{p'}^N(S_{p'}^k): |sum_{ij} m(s_i - s_j) tr(a_ij b_ji)| <= ||T_m||_{cb,p} ||a||_p ||b||_{p'}.

locator.where: Lemma 4.1, line 449 (locally compact groups, 1 < p < infinity with p/p' rational; on R^n explicit Gaussians give every 1 <= p <= infinity, with the L1-normalised Gaussian the narrower one at p = infinity and the wider one at p = 1); Theorem 4.2 proof lines 494-522

targets.name: SchattenClasses.fourierSchurTransference
targets.statement: For every m in Linf(R^n) and 1 <= p <= infinity: ||S_{M_m}||_{cb,p} = ||T_m||_{cb,p}; moreover ||S_{M_m}||_p <= ||T_m||_{cb,p} and ||T_m||_p <= ||S_{M_m}||_p.

locator.where: (FS), lines 71-72; caspers-delasalle-2015 Theorem 4.2 (line 485), Theorem 5.2 (line 543), Corollary 5.3 (line 626); neuwirth-ricard-2011 Theorem 2.7, line 516

targets.name: SchattenClasses.bmoColumn
targets.statement: For f : R^n -> S_2(H) locally square integrable, ||f||_{BMO^c} = sup over cubes Q of || avg_Q |f(z) - f_Q|^2 dz ||^(1/2) (operator norm, |g|^2 = g* g); ||f||_{BMO^r} = ||f*||_{BMO^c}; ||f||_BMO = max. The same on the torus UnitAddTorus (Fin n) with cubes of side at most 1.

api.name: bmo_seminorm
api.statement: seminorm vanishing on constants

api.name: bmo_inf_constants
api.statement: avg_Q |f - alpha|^2 = avg_Q |f - f_Q|^2 + |f_Q - alpha|^2, so the infimum over constants is attained at f_Q

api.name: bmo_le_sup
api.statement: operator Jensen |avg g|^2 <= avg |g|^2, hence ||f||_{BMO^c} <= ess sup ||f(z)||

api.name: bmo_invariance
api.statement: translations, dilations, reflection, and f -> U f V with unitaries

api.name: bmo_dyadic
api.statement: for mean-zero f on the torus, sup_k ||E_k |f - E_{k-1} f|^2||^(1/2) <= 2^(n/2) ||f||_{BMO^c(T^n)}

tests.name: bmo_column_row
tests.statement: f = sum_{k=1}^N 1_{I_k} E_{k1} on T with I_k = [(k-1)/N, k/N), N >= 3: with a_k = |Q cap I_k|/|Q|, avg_Q |f - f_Q|^2 = (1 - sum a_k^2) E_11, so ||f||_{BMO^c} = (1 - 1/N)^(1/2) (at Q = T); avg_Q |f* - f*_Q|^2 = diag(a) - a a^T of norm <= 1/2 (Popoviciu), = 1/2 at Q = I_1 cup I_2, so ||f||_{BMO^r} = 2^(-1/2); N = 4: 0.866 against 0.707; |g|^2 = g g* would exchange them

tests.name: bmo_indicator
tests.statement: f = 1_{[0,1/2)} e on T: on Q = T, avg |f - f_Q|^2 = e/4, value 1/2; unnormalised integrals would grow with the cube

tests.name: bmo_constant
tests.statement: constants have seminorm 0; z -> U_z has column seminorm <= 1

targets.name: SchattenClasses.matrixBMO
targets.statement: For A in S_2(L2(R^n)), pi(A)(z) = U_z A U_z* with U_z multiplication by e^{2 pi i <z, x>}; ||A||_{BMO_c} = ||pi(A)||_{BMO^c(R^n)}, ||A||_{BMO_r} = ||A*||_{BMO_c}, ||A||_BMO = max.

api.name: pi_hom
api.statement: pi is multiplicative and *-preserving with ||pi(A)(z)||_p = ||A||_p

api.name: matrixBMO_norm
api.statement: ||.||_BMO is a norm on S_2 (a Hilbert-Schmidt operator commuting with all U_z is 0)

api.name: matrixBMO_invariance
api.statement: pi(D_u A D_v) = D_u pi(A) D_v; translations, modulations, unitary dilations and reflection preserve ||.||_BMO

api.name: pi_schur
api.statement: pi(S_M A)(z) = S_M(pi(A)(z))

tests.name: matrixBMO_dilation
tests.statement: U_z D_t = D_t U_{z/t}, so pi(D_t A D_t*)(z) = D_t pi(A)(z/t) D_t*

tests.name: matrixBMO_translation
tests.statement: tau_a U_z = e^{-2 pi i <z,a>} U_z tau_a, so pi(tau_a A tau_a*) = tau_a pi(A) tau_a*

tests.name: matrixBMO_wrong_model
tests.statement: pi'(A)(z) = U_z A has column seminorm ||A|| for every A, so it reproduces the operator norm

targets.name: SchattenClasses.periodisation
targets.statement: m_k(x) = floor(8^k x) in Z^n, p_k = 8^{-k} m_k, pi_k(A)(s) = W_{k,s} A W_{k,s}* with W_{k,s} multiplication by e^{2 pi i <s, m_k(x)>}, J_k the Schur multiplier with symbol 1_{|x-y| >= 2^{-k}}. Then ||pi_k(B)||_{Lp(Linf(T^n) (x) B(L2))} = ||B||_p; pi_k J_k = J_k pi_k and pi_k(J_k B) has mean zero when 4^k >= sqrt n; for 4^k >= 4 sqrt n, ||pi_k J_k(A)||_{BMO^c(T^n)} <= ||pi J_k(A)||_{BMO^c(R^n)} + C_n 2^{-k} ||J_k A||_2 (and rows); ||A - J_k A||_2 -> 0 and ||A||_p <= liminf ||J_k A||_p.

locator.where: lines 348-378; Lemma 1.3, line 379, proof lines 380-454; line 506

api.name: pi_k_isometry
api.statement: ||pi_k(B)(s)||_p = ||B||_p and the Bochner Lp norm equals ||B||_p

api.name: pi_k_meanZero
api.statement: for 4^k >= sqrt n, int pi_k(J_k B)(s) ds = 0

api.name: periodisation_bmo
api.statement: the BMO comparison on the torus

api.name: J_k_limit
api.statement: ||A - J_k A||_2 -> 0 and ||A||_p <= liminf ||J_k A||_p

tests.name: periodisation_threshold
tests.statement: n = 2, k = 0: x = (0.05,0.05), y = (0.95,0.95) in the unit cube with |x - y| = 0.9 sqrt 2 >= 1: J_0 keeps the entry while m_0(x) - m_0(y) = 0, so the mean-zero property fails at k = 0

tests.name: periodisation_one_dim
tests.statement: n = 1, k = 0: a kernel in [0,1)^2 has frequencies 0 and is killed by J_0

tests.name: periodisation_rank_one
tests.statement: u (x) v* with u, v in grid cubes labelled a, b: pi_k(u (x) v*)(s) = e^{2 pi i <s, a - b>} u (x) v*, mean zero iff a != b

targets.name: SchattenClasses.matrixBMO_interpolation
targets.statement: There is C_n such that for 2 <= p < infinity and Psi(z) = sum_j e^{delta z^2 + lambda_j z} A_j (finitely many A_j in S_2(L2(R^n)), delta >= 0, lambda_j real): ||Psi(2/p)||_p <= C_n p max(sup_t ||Psi(it)||_BMO, sup_t ||Psi(1+it)||_2). Operator form: if T : S_2 -> S_2 with ||T A||_2 <= C_2 ||A||_2 and ||T A||_BMO <= C_inf ||A|| for finite-rank A, then ||T A||_p <= C_n p C_inf^(1-2/p) C_2^(2/p) ||A||_p.

locator.where: Theorem 1.1, line 313; (1.1) and proof lines 485-539; Lemma 1.2, line 326

targets.name: SchattenClasses.hmsNorm
targets.statement: For sigma_n = floor(n/2) + 1 and M of class C^{sigma_n} on {x != y} in R^n x R^n: |||M|||_HMS = sum_{k=0}^{sigma_n} ess sup_{x != y} |x - y|^k (||D_x^k M(x,y)|| + ||D_y^k M(x,y)||) in [0, infinity], with Frechet derivatives (iteratedFDeriv).

api.name: hms_sup
api.statement: ||M||_inf <= |||M|||/2; M defines a class in Linf

api.name: hms_symmetry
api.statement: |||M^t||| = |||conj M||| = |||Mtilde||| = |||M|||; invariant under M(t x + a, t y + a), t > 0, and common orthogonal changes of variables

api.name: hms_toeplitz
api.statement: |||M_m||| = 2 sum_{k <= sigma_n} sup_xi |xi|^k ||D^k m(xi)||

api.name: hms_multiindex
api.statement: comparable to the multi-index form with constants depending on n

tests.name: hms_phi
tests.statement: n = 1, M = phi(x - y), phi(xi) = xi/sqrt(1 + xi^2): |||M||| = 2 + 4/(3 sqrt 3), same for phi(t xi)

tests.name: hms_sin
tests.statement: M = sin x_1: |||M||| = infinity while ||S_M||_p = 1

tests.name: hms_order
tests.statement: sigma_1 = 1, sigma_2 = 2, sigma_3 = 2, sigma_4 = 3

targets.name: SchattenClasses.twistedFourierMultiplier
targets.statement: For bounded measurable N, the column-twisted multiplier on L2(R^n; S_2(L2(R^n))) is the Fourier multiplier in z with symbol N(x, xi) on the entry (x,y), and the row-twisted one has symbol N(xi, y); M_c(x,xi) = M(x, x - xi), M_r(xi,y) = M(y - xi, y). Norm <= ||N||_inf; right (left) module map with the column (row) L2 bound; localised intertwining: T^c_{M_c}(pi(A) 1_{Q_R}) - avg_Q -> pi(S_M A) - avg_Q in L2(Q; S_2) as R -> infinity, and the row analogue.
hypotheses: N bounded measurable; M as in 11.1 for the intertwining

api.name: twisted_module
api.statement: T^c_N(f E) = (T^c_N f) E and the column bound ||int |T^c_N f|^2||^(1/2) <= ||N||_inf ||int |f|^2||^(1/2)

api.name: twisted_intertwine
api.statement: localised T^c_{M_c}(pi(A)) = pi(S_M A) modulo constants on every cube

tests.name: twisted_toeplitz
tests.statement: Toeplitz M_m: M_c = m(xi) independent of x, the ordinary multiplier T_m entrywise with T_m e_{x-y} = m(x-y) e_{x-y}

tests.name: twisted_identity
tests.statement: N = 1 gives the identity

tests.name: twisted_row_function
tests.statement: M(x,y) = f(x): T^c_{M_c} is left multiplication by D_f and S_M(A) = D_f A

targets.name: SchattenClasses.littlewoodPaley_uniform
targets.statement: With psi_j(xi) = phi(2^{-j} xi) - phi(2^{1-j} xi), N(x,.) of class C^{sigma_n} off 0 with B = sup_x sum_{k <= sigma_n} sup_xi |xi|^k ||D^k_xi N(x,xi)|| finite and k_j(x,.) = F^{-1}(psi_j N(x,.)): int |s|^{2 sigma_n} |k_j(x,s)|^2 ds <= C_n B^2 2^{j(n - 2 sigma_n)}, int |grad k_j|^2 <= C_n ||N||_inf^2 2^{j(n+2)}, int |s|^{2 sigma_n} |grad k_j|^2 <= C_n B^2 2^{j(n + 2 - 2 sigma_n)}.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.schurMultiplier_bmo_endpoint
targets.statement: For M as in 11.1 and A in S_2(L2(R^n)): ||S_M A||_{BMO_c} <= C_n (sum_{k <= sigma_n} ess sup |x - y|^k ||D_y^k M||) ||A|| and ||S_M A||_{BMO_r} <= C_n (sum ess sup |x - y|^k ||D_x^k M||) ||A||; hence ||S_M A||_BMO <= C_n |||M|||_HMS ||A||.

targets.name: SchattenClasses.hormanderMikhlinSchur
targets.statement: There is C_n such that for 1 < p < infinity and M of class C^{sigma_n} on {x != y} with |||M|||_HMS finite: ||S_M||_{S_p(L2(R^n)) -> S_p(L2(R^n))} = ||S_M||_{cb,p} <= C_n (p^2/(p-1)) |||M|||_HMS.

locator.where: Theorem A, lines 149-154; step 1, lines 565-571; Remark 2.1, line 1042; grafakos-classical-2014 Theorem 6.2.7 (uncertified)

suppliers.what: Approximation numbers, finite-rank approximability and compactness, adjoint invariance, localisation on finite-dimensional subspaces; trace-class, Hilbert-Schmidt and Schatten families with inclusions; the Hilbert-Schmidt column model (implemented in Tau Ceti as TauCeti.OperatorIdealFamily.*).
The canonical trace with cyclicity, rank-one formulas and B(H) = S_1(H)*; L2(mu) (x) L2(nu) = L2(mu x nu); the Hilbert-space ultraproduct of a sequence of Hilbert spaces.

Finite-rank density, Hoelder, Lp(B(H),Tr) = S_p, Lp-Lq duality, the complex method with regularisation, interpolation of semifinite Lp couples, noncommutative Riesz-Thorin, Bochner Lp(Omega; Lp(N)); the semifinite martingale BMO interpolation inequality is requested of its Part II.

The L2 kernel operator with kernel_apply, kernel_unique, kernel_norm; the complex trace; kernel_trace_diagonal; requested at the generality of arbitrary sigma-finite measure spaces (gap sigma-finite-hilbert-schmidt-kernels).
The C*-algebra of compact operators; completely bounded maps of operator spaces (comparison at p = infinity).
Bochner density of a vector measure of bounded variation in a reflexive space (Radon-Nikodym representation of L1(mu) -> K).

consumers.what: Proposed: Sobolev form of the Hormander-Mikhlin-Schur theorem (cgpt-2023 Theorem A'), Calderon-Torchinsky variants, divided differences of alpha-Hoelder functions and Arazy's conjecture, discrete and Lie-group formulations; consumes Layers 3, 4, 7, 10, 11.
Proposed: Schur multipliers with divided-difference symbols on spectral measure spaces (potapov-sukochev-2011 Theorems 1 and 7); consumes Layers 2-4 and 11.
Proposed: Lafforgue-de la Salle §2 onwards, the constants Lambda^Schur_{p,cb}; consumes Layers 3-8.
Proposed: Neuwirth-Ricard and Caspers-de la Salle transference beyond R^n; consumes Layers 3, 8, 9.

gaps.title: Hilbert-Schmidt kernel operators on arbitrary sigma-finite measure spaces
gaps.detail: AutomorphicSpectralTheory §0.8 states the kernel operator T_K, kernel_apply, kernel_unique and kernel_norm on sigma-finite standard Borel spaces with separable L2, and §0.10 the trace formula Tr(T_1 T_2) = int int K_1(x,y) K_2(y,x). Layers 2, 5 and 7 need them for arbitrary sigma-finite measure spaces, including sub-sigma-algebras of a standard Borel space, which are not standard Borel. A route without countable orthonormal bases: VonNeumannAlgebras V2.RectangularL2 composed with the unitary S_2(L2(nu), L2(mu)) = L2(mu) (x) conj(L2(nu)) of V4.Core, identified with the integral formula on rank-one kernels and extended by continuity.
gaps.needs: For arbitrary sigma-finite measure spaces (X, mu) and (Y, nu), with no standard Borel or separability hypothesis: the kernel operator T_K : L2(Y, nu) -> L2(X, mu), T_K f(x) = int K(x, y) f(y) dnu(y) for almost every x, of every K in L2(mu x nu), with K -> T_K a linear embedding of L2(mu x nu) into the bounded operators, isometric for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm: ||T_K||_HS = ||K||_2 (§0.8: kernel_apply, kernel_unique, kernel_norm), and Tr(T_1 T_2) = int int K_1(x, y) K_2(y, x) dmu(x) dmu(y) for K_1, K_2 in L2(mu x mu) (§0.10, first assertion).

gaps.title: Interpolation between semifinite operator-valued martingale BMO and L2 with constant O(p)
gaps.detail: For N semifinite, a filtration (F_k) of a probability space with F_0 trivial generating F, M = Linf(Omega) (x) N with trace int (x) tau_N, E_k = E[.|F_k] (x) id, E_{-1} = 0, ||f||_{BMO_c} = sup_k ||E_k |f - E_{k-1} f|^2||^(1/2), BMO_r via f*, BMO = max: there is an absolute C such that for 2 <= p < infinity and every Psi(z) = sum_j e^{delta z^2 + lambda_j z} f_j (f_j in L2 cap M of mean zero, delta >= 0, lambda_j real), ||Psi(2/p)||_p <= C p max(sup_t ||Psi(it)||_BMO, sup_t ||Psi(1+it)||_2). Sources: cgpt-2023 Lemma 1.4 (lines 471-484) for the dyadic filtration of T^n with N = B(L2(R^n)); mei-2007 Lemma 6.1 (line 3218) for semifinite operator-valued dyadic filtrations with equivalent norms; musat-2003 Theorem 3.1 (uncertified); jrwz-2020 (uncertified) for the order O(1/(q-1)) of the Burkholder-Gundy constant. NoncommutativeIntegration owns finite-tracial H1-BMO duality (§8.4) and Burkholder-Gundy with constants depending only on p (§7.3); the semifinite operator-valued version with the sharp order is in its direction.
gaps.needs: For a semifinite von Neumann algebra (N, tau_N), a probability space (Omega, F, P) with a filtration (F_k)_{k >= 0}, F_0 trivial, generating F, the algebra M = Linf(Omega) (x) N with the trace int (x) tau_N, E_k = E[. | F_k] (x) id_N and E_{-1} = 0: the norms ||f||_{BMO_c} = sup_{k >= 0} ||E_k |f - E_{k-1} f|^2||^{1/2}, ||f||_{BMO_r} = ||f*||_{BMO_c} and ||f||_BMO = max(||f||_{BMO_c}, ||f||_{BMO_r}) on L2(M) cap M, and an absolute constant C such that ||Psi(2/p)||_{Lp(M)} <= C p max(sup_t ||Psi(it)||_BMO, sup_t ||Psi(1 + it)||_{L2(M)}) for every 2 <= p < infinity and every Psi(z) = sum_j e^{delta z^2 + lambda_j z} f_j on the strip 0 <= Re z <= 1 with finitely many f_j in L2(M) cap M, E_0 f_j = 0, delta >= 0 and lambda_j real.
